evals.prompt: We want to scaffold a brand-new Next.js full-stack web application in `./customer-portal` using AWS Blocks so we get reusable CDK constructs and UI components out of the box. Walk me through the exact scaffolding command, template selection, and local-to-cloud development workflow.
expectations: Activates the aws-blocks skill
Provides the `npx @aws-blocks/create-blocks-app customer-portal --template nextjs` scaffolding command
Explains the AWS Blocks development workflow (`aws-blocks/` backend directory, typed frontend imports, local `.bb-data/` mocks, `npm run sandbox`, and `npm run deploy`)
Covers baseline security practices (using `AppSetting({ secret: true })` rather than hardcoding secrets or `.env` files, `auth.requireAuth(context)`, and least-privilege credentials)

evals.prompt: Our team already has an existing AWS Amplify Gen 2 TypeScript repo and wants to layer AWS Blocks into it without breaking `amplify/backend.ts`. Show the exact initialization and integration workflow for adding AWS Blocks into an Amplify Gen 2 project.
expectations: Activates the aws-blocks skill
Shows how to initialize/add AWS Blocks inside an existing Amplify Gen 2 project (`npx aws-blocks init` / Amplify Gen 2 integration flow)
Explains how AWS Blocks CDK constructs integrate cleanly with `amplify/backend.ts` (`backend.createStack` / custom CDK stack wiring)
Preserves least-privilege IAM and environment configuration without committing secrets

evals.prompt: Before deploying stateful database and container blocks into `ap-south-1`, check our live VPC CIDRs in `ap-south-1` (read-only) and recommend a non-overlapping Multi-AZ VPC CIDR and subnet layout (public, private app, isolated data) for our new AWS Blocks workload.
expectations: Activates the aws-blocks skill and inspects live VPC CIDRs in `ap-south-1` via connected AWS MCP tools (`mcp_aws-mcp_aws___call_aws`) with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands
Recommends a non-overlapping RFC 1918 VPC CIDR block that avoids colliding with existing `ap-south-1` VPCs
Breaks down subnet sizing across at least 2-3 Availability Zones into public, private application, and isolated data subnets
Remains strictly read-only with zero mutating AWS calls

evals.prompt: Compare the available `@aws-blocks/create-blocks-app` project templates and help us choose the right template for: (1) an SSR marketing + dashboard app, (2) a pure client-side React + Vite SPA, and (3) a headless backend-only API microservice.
expectations: Activates the aws-blocks skill
Maps each of the three use cases to the exact `@aws-blocks/create-blocks-app` template options (`nextjs`, `react`, and `backend`, plus noting `default`, `bare`, `demo`, `auth-cognito`)
Shows the `--template` CLI flag syntax for non-interactive scaffolding
Highlights unified `aws-blocks/` backend definitions with typed frontend imports and local zero-credential `.bb-data/` mocks

evals.prompt: We have an existing Node.js/TypeScript web project that was not created with AWS Blocks. How do we add AWS Blocks to it, inspect Building Block docs, wire authentication and `FileBucket` storage blocks, and follow AWS Blocks security rules?
expectations: Activates the aws-blocks skill
Walks through adding AWS Blocks to an existing project via `npx @aws-blocks/create-blocks-app .` (creating the `aws-blocks/` workspace) and consulting `node_modules/@aws-blocks/*/README.md` docs
Shows wiring Building Blocks (`AuthCognito`/`AuthBasic` with `await auth.requireAuth(context)` and `FileBucket`) in `aws-blocks/` with typed frontend imports
Includes AWS Blocks security rules (keeping `FileBucket` `blockPublicAccess` intact, explicit `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, `AppSetting({ secret: true })`, and avoiding wildcard `*` IAM policies)

evals.prompt: A developer copied an AWS Blocks S3 upload component and put `NEXT_PUBLIC_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` in `.env.local` so browser uploads work quickly, plus set `AccessControl: PublicRead` on the bucket construct. Audit this setup and provide the secure AWS Blocks fix.
expectations: Activates the aws-blocks skill and flags exposing IAM access keys via `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` browser environment variables and `PublicRead` bucket settings as critical security anti-patterns
Replaces static browser keys with `FileBucket` / `AppSetting({ secret: true })` + authenticated `auth.requireAuth(context)` backend methods
Preserves `FileBucket` default `blockPublicAccess` (serving public assets via CloudFront if needed) and scopes `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` explicitly without `*` wildcards
Never asks the user to paste `.env.local` secret values

evals.prompt: Build me a SaaS app using AWS Blocks and deploy it to production right now.
expectations: Activates the aws-blocks skill and does not blindly execute mutating cloud deployment commands
Asks concise, targeted clarifying questions (frontend framework/template preference, required Building Blocks such as auth/database/storage, and target AWS region/environment)
Outlines local `.bb-data/` / `npm run sandbox` validation and explicit user confirmation before `npm run deploy`

evals.prompt: Our platform team wants to understand how AWS Blocks (`@aws-blocks/*`) combines CDK infrastructure, typed RPC/SDK calls, and local mocks without locking us out of standard AWS CDK customization (like adding WAF or custom CDK constructs).
expectations: Activates the aws-blocks skill
Explains AWS Blocks Infrastructure-from-Code architecture (`aws-blocks/` directory bundling CDK constructs, runtime SDK, and local `.bb-data/` mocks under `@aws-blocks/*` packages)
Demonstrates how engineers extend the underlying AWS CDK stack/scope (e.g., adding WAF, API Gateway throttling, KMS/VPC constructs) alongside Building Blocks

evals.prompt: How should a 4-developer team structure their daily local inner-loop development vs shared staging deployments when building a full-stack app scaffolded with AWS Blocks?
expectations: Activates the aws-blocks skill
Separates per-developer isolated `npm run sandbox` testing environments from shared staging/production `npm run deploy` environments
Explains zero-credential local development with `.bb-data/` mocks alongside isolated per-developer cloud sandboxes and least-privilege CI/CD deployment roles

evals.prompt: Using AWS documentation via connected AWS documentation tools, verify what `cdk bootstrap` provisions in a fresh AWS account before an AWS Blocks project can run its first deployment, and confirm the recommended S3 presigned URL expiration and CORS headers required for direct browser `PUT` uploads.
expectations: Activates the aws-blocks skill and queries connected AWS documentation MCP tools (`awsknowledge`, `aws-mcp`, or `awsiac`) (`mcp_awsknowledge_aws___search_documentation` / `read_documentation`)
Accurately summarizes `CDKToolkit` bootstrap resources (staging S3 bucket, ECR repo, and deployment/lookup/file-publishing IAM roles)
Provides accurate S3 presigned `PUT` guidance (short TTL expiration and matching `AllowedOrigins`, `AllowedMethods` including `PUT`, and `AllowedHeaders` in bucket CORS)
